title: CodeQuant: Unified Clustering and Quantization for Enhanced Outlier Smoothing in Low-Precision Mixture-of-Experts
claim: A complex system decomposes into four coordinated stages, each targeting a distinct source of error, from smoothing through deployment.
layout: Left architecture insets, then four colored stage boxes flowing left-to-right with feedback arrows
description: A wide figure titled 'CodeQuant Framework'. On the left, two dashed-zoom insets show a MoE FFN block (Linear, SiLU, weighted sum, experts 0..n, router, layernorm) and a self-attention block (Wq, Wk, Wv, softmax, Wout), both linked to a central rounded box listing the FFN and SA layers with input X. From there, four color-coded rounded boxes follow. Stage 1 (green) shows the argmin ||X - Q(XR)||^2 objective and two 3D heatmaps, spiky outliers before and uniform after rotation. Stage 2 (red, below) shows permutation-invariant outlier grouping with weight matrices Wv and Wo. Stage 3 (blue) shows clustering and centroid finetuning with Y, Wc, W, C, A blocks. Stage 4 (orange) shows a LUT-based kernel with centroid lookup tables, multipliers and a MUX. Black arrows connect the stages.
caption: Overview of the CodeQuant framework. The left panel illustrates the target architectures, including MoE FFN and Self-Attention blocks. The right panel depicts the four-stage calibration and deployment pipeline: Stage 1 applies learnable rotations to smooth activation outliers; Stage 2 permute weight for optimized distribution; Stage 3 introduces clustering fine-tune mechanism to align with objective; and Stage 4 deploys the quantized model using a specialized LUT kernel.
abstract: Outliers have emerged as a fundamental bottleneck in preserving accuracy for low-precision large models, particularly within Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures that are increasingly central to large-scale language modeling. Under post-training quantization (PTQ), these outliers induce substantial quantization errors, leading to severe accuracy degradation. While recent rotation-based smoothing techniques alleviate the problem by redistributing outlier magnitudes, residual errors remain and continue to impede reliable low-precision deployment. In this work, we tackle this challenge by introducing CodeQuant, a unified quantization-and-clustering scheme that contains smoothing activation outliers via learnable rotation and absorbing weight outliers into fine-tuned cluster centroids for MoE. This design reduces the influence of extreme values by fitting them within cluster centroids, thereby lowering quantization error while maintaining expressive capacity. Coupled with a dedicated kernel design for GPU and CPU, CodeQuant achieves up to $4.15\times$ speedup while delivering significantly higher accuracy than state-of-the-art quantization approaches across diverse MoE models. Our results highlight CodeQuant as a promising direction for efficient and accurate deployment of MoE-based large language models under low-precision constraints. Our code is available at https://github.com/SAI-Lab-NYU/CodeQuant.
